raw_response:
I've been working this land for twenty years and I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, well water is reliable, and my body isn't as strong as it used to be at 68, so I don't want to overcomplicatethe season.

My main fields — about 4.5 mu — run the wheat-maize rotation like always. Wheat goes in October, maize follows after the June harvest. Same land, two crops a year. The remaining 3 mu I split between my vegetables: cabbage takes the biggest chunk since it sells well in autumn, and I keep a little ground for chili and eggplant.

For wheat, I'll use the hybrid seed I've bought from the county supply cooperative for the past several years. Works fine. I put down base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing stage. I irrigate four times — before sowing, at jointing, heading, and grain filling. That's what the soil needs here.

For maize, I sow right after wheat harvest in June. I go no-tillage to save time and my back. I water it three times and put more nitrogen down because maize drinks it up.

Vegetables get more attention. Cabbage in late July on 1.5 mu — rotary till first, transplant seedlings, water often because August is dry. Chili and eggplant go in on the smaller plots in spring. I keep those varieties I've used before — the local chili is what buyers around here want.

I won't change much this year. My yields have been stable. My grandchildren are in school and need feeding. Steady is better than risky.
